source_text: βαλα εἶναι, ἵνα Χριστὸν κερδήσω, καὶ εὑρεθῶ ἐν αὐτῷ μὴ ἔχων ἐμὴν δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐν νόμῳ, ἀλλὰ τὴν διὰ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ;» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἐπυθόμην. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἐπετίμα δὲ καὶ ἑτέροις, ὡς τὴν ἐν νόμῳ τετιμηκόσι περιτομὴν μετὰ τὸ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον. «Κατηργήθητε γὰρ ἀπὸ Χριστοῦ, φησὶν, οἵτινες ἐν νόμῳ δικαιοῦσθε, τῆς χάριτος ἐξεπέσετε. Ἡμεῖς δὲ διὰ πίστεως ἐλπίδα δικαιοσύνης ἀπεκδεχόμεθα.» Ἠχρειῶσθαι δὲ καὶ τὴν ἀρχαίαν ἐκείνην ἔφασκεν ἐντολὴν, οὐκ ἀμωμήτως ἔχουσαν, ἀντεισῆχθαι δὲ τὴν ἑτέραν, τουτέστι τὴν εὐαγγελικήν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀργοτέραν οὖν ἄρα τὴν ἐν νόμῳ παίδευσιν ἀποφαίνει τὸ αἴνιγμα, ξυρᾶσθαι κελεῦον τὸν εὐξάμενον Ἰσραὴλ, ὡς μολυσμὸν ὑπομείναντα τὸν ἐπὶ νεκρῷ, τουτέστι, τὸν τοῖς τῆς κυριοκτονίας ἐνισχημένον ἐγκλήμασι, κόμην δὲ ὥσπερ ἑτέραν ἁγιάζειν Θεῷ μετὰ τὴν ὀγδόην, τουτέστι, μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν, τῶν εὐαγγελικῶν θεσπισμάτων τὴν ἀκριβῆ καὶ τετορευμένην ἀστειότητά τε καὶ παίδευσιν. Τῷ γε μὴν τρέφοντι τὴν τρίχα, μετὰ τὴν ὀγδόην, τρυγόνας προσάγειν καὶ περιστερὰς ὁ νόμος προστέταχε, μήνυσιν ὥσπερ καὶ τοῦτο τιθεὶς τοῦ καθαίροντος τοὺς μεμολυσμένους, τουτέστι, Χριστοῦ. Σημαίνεται γὰρ δι' ἀμφοῖν, ὡς εὐφωνότατος μὲν ἐν τρυγόνι, πραότατος δὲ διὰ τῆς περιστερᾶς· καὶ τοιούτου νόμου βραδυγλώσσου τε ὄντος, καὶ τὸ πρᾶον οὐκ ἔχοντος. Ἐπιτίθησι γὰρ εὐθὺς τοῖς πλημμελοῦσι τὰς δίκας. Ἀναφέρεται δὲ καὶ ἀμνὸς τοῖς στρουθίοις ὁμοῦ, ἵνα διὰ πάντων νοοῖτο Χριστὸς, ὡς διὰ μὲν τῶν στρουθίων, ἄνωθεν καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, διὰ δὲ τοῦ ἀμνοῦ, κάτωθεν καὶ ἀπὸ γῆς. Θεὸς γὰρ ὑπάρχων κατὰ φύσιν ὁ Λόγος, γέγονε σάρξ. Ἀλλ' ἦν καὶ ἔστι καὶ οὕτω Θεός· καὶ ἀπαλλάττει μὲν ἡμᾶς τῆς κατὰ νόμον σκιᾶς, ἐνίησι δὲ ταῖς ἁπάντων καρδίαις τῶν ἑαυτοῦ θεσπισμάτων τὴν εἴδησιν· καὶ ἁγίους ἀληθῶς ἀποφαίνει, τῷ ἰδίῳ καθαίρων αἵματι, κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὧδε ἔχει. {ΚΥΡ.} Εἰ δὲ δὴ, φησὶν, ἀποπεραίνοιτο καλῶς ὁ τῆς εὐχῆς τρόπος, τῷ κομῶντι μετὰ τὴν ὀγδόην, τελειούσθω τότε· καὶ ὅπως ἔσται τὸ χρῆμα, νομοθετεῖ λέγων· «Καὶ οὗτος ὁ νόμος τοῦ εὐξαμένου· Ἦ ἂν ἡμέρᾳ πληρώσῃ ἡμέρας εὐχῆς αὐτοῦ, προσοίσει αὐτὸς παρὰ τὰς θύρας τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου· καὶ προσάξει τὸ δῶρον αὐτοῦ Κυρίῳ ἀμνὸν ἐνιαύσιον ἄμωμον ἕνα εἰς ὁλοκαύτωσιν, καὶ ἀμνάδα ἐνιαυσίαν μίαν ἄμωμον εἰς ἁμαρτίαν, καὶ κριὸν ἕνα ἄμωμον εἰς σωτήριον, καὶ κανοῦν ἀζύμων σεμιδάλεως, ἄρτους ἀναπεποιημένους ἐν ἐλαίῳ, καὶ λάγανα ἄζυμα κεχρισμένα ἐν ἐλαίῳ, καὶ θυσίαν αὐτῶν, καὶ σπονδὴν αὐτῶν, καὶ προσοίσει ὁ ἱερεὺς ἔναντι Κυρίου, καὶ ποιήσει τὸ περὶ ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ ὁλοκαύτωμα αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸν κριὸν ποιήσει θυσίαν σωτηρίου τῷ Κυρίῳ ἐπὶ τοῦ κανοῦ τῶν ἀζύμων. Καὶ ποιήσει ὁ
pass_a_gloss: Cyril (end of the quotation): '[dung] to be, that I may gain Christ, and be found in him not having my own righteousness, the one in law, but the one through faith of Jesus Christ?' Palladius: I have learned it (ἐπυθόμην). Cyril: And he also rebuked others, as having honored the circumcision in law after the mystery of Christ. 'For you were cut off (κατηργήθητε) from Christ,' he says, 'you who are being justified in law; you fell from grace. But we through faith await the hope of righteousness.' And he said that that ancient commandment (ἐντολή) had also been made useless (ἠχρειῶσθαι), not holding itself blamelessly, and that the other had been brought in instead (ἀντεισῆχθαι), that is, the gospel one. Palladius: True. Cyril: The riddle (αἴνιγμα) then shows the training in law to be idler (ἀργοτέραν), bidding the Israel that vowed to be shaved, as having undergone the defilement over a dead body, that is, as the one held fast in the charges of the Lord-killing, and to sanctify to God as it were another head of hair after the eighth, that is, after the resurrection: the exact and finely chased (τετορευμένην) refinement (ἀστειότης) and training of the gospel decrees (θεσπίσματα). To the one nourishing the hair, after the eighth, the law has ordered to bring turtledoves and doves, setting this too as it were as an indication (μήνυσις) of the one who cleanses the defiled, that is, of Christ. For he is signified through both: as most sweet-voiced (εὐφωνότατος) in the turtledove, and gentlest (πραότατος) through the dove; and the law being such, both slow of tongue (βραδύγλωσσος) and not having the gentle. For it at once lays the penalties (δίκαι) on those who offend. And a lamb (ἀμνός) is also brought up together with the small birds, so that through all of them Christ may be understood: through the birds as from above and from heaven, through the lamb as from below and from the earth. For being God by nature, the Word (Λόγος) became flesh. But he was and is God even so; and he frees us from the shadow according to the law, and puts into the hearts of all the knowledge of his own decrees; and he makes [us] truly holy, cleansing with his own blood, according to the Scriptures. Palladius: Thus it holds. Cyril: And if indeed, he says, the manner (τρόπος) of the vow should be brought to completion well by the one wearing long hair after the eighth, let him then be perfected (τελειούσθω); and how the matter will be, he legislates, saying: 'And this is the law of the one who vowed: on whatever day he fulfills the days of his vow, he himself shall bring [himself] beside the doors of the tent of witness; and he shall bring his gift to the Lord: one unblemished year-old lamb for a whole burnt offering (ὁλοκαύτωσις), and one unblemished year-old ewe lamb for sin, and one unblemished ram for salvation (σωτήριον), and a basket of unleavened [loaves] of fine flour, loaves kneaded in oil, and unleavened wafers (λάγανα) anointed in oil, and their sacrifice and their libation; and the priest shall bring [them] before the Lord, and shall make his [offering] for sin and his whole burnt offering, and he shall make the ram a sacrifice of salvation to the Lord upon the basket of the unleavened. And the' [the column breaks before 'priest'].

(end of quotation) ‘[σκύ]βαλα εἶναι (to be dung/rubbish), ἵνα Χριστὸν κερδήσω, καὶ εὑρεθῶ ἐν αὐτῷ μὴ ἔχων ἐμὴν δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐν νόμῳ, ἀλλὰ τὴν διὰ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ’ — question ends. ΠΑΛΛ. ἐπυθόμην (I have learned/heard). ΚΥΡ. ἐπετίμα (he rebuked) others as having honored τὴν ἐν νόμῳ περιτομήν after τὸ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον: ‘κατηργήθητε ἀπὸ Χριστοῦ (you were severed from Christ), οἵτινες ἐν νόμῳ δικαιοῦσθε (who are being justified in law), τῆς χάριτος ἐξεπέσετε (fell from grace); ἡμεῖς δὲ διὰ πίστεως ἐλπίδα δικαιοσύνης ἀπεκδεχόμεθα (await)’. He said the old ἐντολή ἠχρειῶσθαι (was made useless), οὐκ ἀμωμήτως ἔχουσαν (not being blameless), and ἀντεισῆχθαι (another brought in instead), i.e. the εὐαγγελική. ΠΑΛΛ. ἀληθές. ΚΥΡ. the αἴνιγμα shows ἀργοτέραν (idler/inactive) the ἐν νόμῳ παίδευσις, ordering the εὐξάμενον Ἰσραήλ to be shaved as having undergone μολυσμὸν τὸν ἐπὶ νεκρῷ, i.e. ἐνισχημένον (held in) the ἐγκλήματα τῆς κυριοκτονίας; and to ἁγιάζειν Θεῷ another κόμη after the eighth, i.e. after the ἀνάστασις: the ἀκριβῆ καὶ τετορευμένην (precise, finely chased) ἀστειότης (refinement) and παίδευσις of the εὐαγγελικὰ θεσπίσματα. To τῷ τρέφοντι τὴν τρίχα after the eighth the law προστέταχε (ordered) to bring τρυγόνας καὶ περιστεράς, a μήνυσις (indication) of the one who καθαίρει (cleanses) the defiled, i.e. Christ; signified by both: εὐφωνότατος (most melodious) in the turtledove, πραότατος (gentlest) through the dove; τοιούτου νόμου βραδυγλώσσου (the law being slow-tongued) and not having τὸ πρᾶον (gentleness); for it ἐπιτίθησι εὐθύς (imposes at once) δίκας on πλημμελοῦσι (offenders). ἀμνός offered with the στρουθία (birds) so Christ is understood through all: birds ἄνωθεν, ἐξ οὐρανοῦ; lamb κάτωθεν, ἀπὸ γῆς. For Θεὸς ὑπάρχων κατὰ φύσιν ὁ Λόγος γέγονε σάρξ; ἀλλ᾽ ἦν καὶ ἔστι καὶ οὕτω Θεός; ἀπαλλάττει (frees) us from τῆς κατὰ νόμον σκιᾶς, ἐνίησι (puts into) all hearts the εἴδησις of his θεσπίσματα; ἁγίους ἀποφαίνει, τῷ ἰδίῳ καθαίρων αἵματι, κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς. ΠΑΛΛ. ὧδε ἔχει. ΚΥΡ. if ἀποπεραίνοιτο καλῶς (be completed well) ὁ τῆς εὐχῆς τρόπος by τῷ κομῶντι after the eighth, τελειούσθω (let him be perfected/completed); νομοθετεῖ: ‘οὗτος ὁ νόμος τοῦ εὐξαμένου; on the day πληρώσῃ ἡμέρας εὐχῆς, προσοίσει αὐτός at the doors of τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου; προσάξει τὸ δῶρον Κυρίῳ: ἀμνὸν ἐνιαύσιον ἄμωμον ἕνα εἰς ὁλοκαύτωσιν, ἀμνάδα ἐνιαυσίαν μίαν ἄμωμον εἰς ἁμαρτίαν, κριὸν ἕνα ἄμωμον εἰς σωτήριον, κανοῦν ἀζύμων σεμιδάλεως, ἄρτους ἀναπεποιημένους ἐν ἐλαίῳ, λάγανα ἄζυμα κεχρισμένα ἐν ἐλαίῳ, θυσίαν αὐτῶν καὶ σπονδὴν αὐτῶν; the priest προσοίσει ἔναντι Κυρίου, ποιήσει τὸ περὶ ἁμαρτίας and τὸ ὁλοκαύτωμα; τὸν κριὸν ποιήσει θυσίαν σωτηρίου τῷ Κυρίῳ ἐπὶ τοῦ κανοῦ τῶν ἀζύμων; καὶ ποιήσει ὁ [ἱερεύς]’ (column breaks).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …rubbish, so that I may gain Christ and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own that is in the law, but the righteousness that comes through faith in Jesus Christ’ (Philippians 3:8–9)?

Cyril: He also rebuked others for honoring the circumcision of the law after the mystery of Christ. ‘You have been cut off from Christ,’ he says, ‘you who would be justified by the law; you have fallen from grace. But we, through faith, await the hope of righteousness’ (Galatians 5:4–5). He said too that the old commandment had been made useless, since it was not without fault, and that the other, that is, the commandment of the Gospel, had been brought in to take its place (Hebrews 7:18–19; Hebrews 8:7).

Cyril: So the riddle shows that the teaching of the law has become idle. It commands Israel, who had made the vow, to be shaved as one who had incurred defilement from a dead body, that is, as one held fast in the guilt of killing the Lord; and to sanctify to God, as it were, another head of hair after the eighth day, that is, after the resurrection: the precise and finely wrought refinement and teaching of the decrees of the Gospel. To the one who grows his hair after the eighth day the law prescribed the offering of turtledoves and doves (Numbers 6:10), setting this down too as a sign of the one who cleanses the defiled, that is, of Christ. For he is signified by both: as most sweet-voiced by the turtledove, as most gentle by the dove; whereas the law is slow of tongue (Exodus 4:10) and has no gentleness, for it punishes wrongdoers at once. A lamb is also offered together with the birds (Numbers 6:12), so that Christ may be understood through them all: through the birds as from above and from heaven, through the lamb as from below and from the earth. For the Word, who is God by nature, became flesh (John 1:14). Yet even so he was and is God. He frees us from the shadow of the law and puts into the hearts of all the knowledge of his own decrees; and he makes us truly holy, cleansing us with his own blood, according to the Scriptures (Hebrews 13:12).

Cyril: But if, he says, the course of the vow is brought to a good end by the one who lets his hair grow after the eighth day, let him then be made complete. And he lays down how this is to be done, saying: ‘And this is the law of the one who has vowed: on the day he completes the days of his vow, he shall present himself at the doors of the tent of witness. And he shall offer his gift to the Lord: one male lamb a year old without blemish for a whole burnt offering, and one ewe lamb a year old without blemish for a sin offering, and one ram without blemish for a peace offering, and a basket of unleavened loaves of fine flour, loaves mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and their grain offering and their drink offering. And the priest shall bring them before the Lord, and shall offer his sin offering and his whole burnt offering; and he shall offer the ram as a sacrifice of peace offering to the Lord, with the basket of unleavened loaves. And the priest shall…’ (Numbers 6:13–17)

apparatus.note: PG OCR; a column may cut mid-sentence or mid-word.
καὶ τοιούτου νόμου βραδυγλώσσου τε ὄντος may be corrupt (perhaps οὐ τοιούτου); rendered 'whereas the law is slow of tongue'. Another edition would settle it.

Opens mid-quotation (σκύ|βαλα) and closes Cyril’s rhetorical question from §22, so the question mark follows the citation. Philippians 3:9: Cyril reads τὴν ἐν νόμῳ (NT: ἐκ νόμου); rendered ‘that is in the law’. Galatians 5:4–5: Cyril reads ‘Ἡμεῖς δὲ διὰ πίστεως’ (NT: ἡμεῖς γὰρ πνεύματι ἐκ πίστεως); translated as Cyril gives it; ‘you who would be justified’ renders the conative present δικαιοῦσθε. The old commandment ‘made useless … not without fault … another brought in’ is Cyril’s paraphrase of Hebrews 7:18–19 (ἀθέτησις … ἀνωφελές; ἐπεισαγωγή) and 8:7 (εἰ ἡ πρώτη ἐκείνη ἦν ἄμεμπτος), which Cyril treats as Paul’s. ‘Slow of tongue’ (βραδύγλωσσος) is the LXX word for Moses in Exodus 4:10; Cyril transfers it to the law given through Moses, so the clause is cited as a clear verbal allusion. Text ‘καὶ τοιούτου νόμου βραδυγλώσσου τε ὄντος’ is awkward (possibly οὐ τοιούτου, ‘the law not being such’); either way the sense is a contrast with Christ, rendered ‘whereas the law is slow of tongue’. ‘Turtledoves and doves after the eighth day’ refers to Numbers 6:10 (‘on the eighth day’); the lamb with the birds is Numbers 6:12. ‘Cleansing us with his own blood, according to the Scriptures’: Cyril signals Scripture without quoting; nearest wording is Hebrews 13:12 (ἵνα ἁγιάσῃ διὰ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος τὸν λαόν), cited; compare 1 John 1:7 and Hebrews 9:14. The turtledove-melody and dove-gentleness figures are uncited (no specific verse quoted). Numbers 6:13–17 follows the LXX: σωτήριον rendered ‘peace offering’ (it also means ‘salvation offering’, a sense Cyril uses in §25); θυσία αὐτῶν rendered ‘grain offering’ as in the verse’s sense; ‘προσοίσει αὐτός’ rendered ‘he shall present himself’. The quotation breaks mid-sentence at the column end (ποιήσει ὁ | ἱερεύς).
